trigger: A cohort has >= kDexCohortFloor reporting devices (suppressed=false) but zero of those devices have a value for one particular metric (each of cpu_pct/commit_pct/disk_lat_ms is parsed independently per device in dex_perf_rules.hpp, so one metric can be universally absent while others report)
summary: get_dex_perf_cohorts/get_dex_perf_cohort_diff's new output schemas typed cpu_pct/commit_pct/disk_lat_ms as plain (non-nullable) object, but the handler's stat_json() helper can emit a literal JSON null for one of these fields even on an unsuppressed cohort (dex_perf_model.cpp:124-126, r.cpu/commit/disk_lat are std::optional and can independently be nullopt). Confirmed empirically by reading dex_perf_model.cpp directly - contradicted architect's/consistency-auditor's initial PASS verdict on the same code path, which only checked the suppressed-vs-unsuppressed binary and missed the per-metric case.
classification_rationale: Advertised output schema does not admit a value shape the handler can legitimately produce.

trigger: Reading the shipped changelog fragment's claim that get_dex_perf_cohort_diff was one of the tools that previously returned a bare JSON array
summary: Fragment claimed 5 bare-array tools including get_dex_perf_cohort_diff; the tool has always built a JObj (never a bare array), both pre- and post-diff. Correct count is 4. Found independently by security-guardian, docs-writer, architect, and consistency-auditor (4 independent reporters) - this commit's own commit message stated the correct count of 4, so the two release-note artifacts in the same commit disagreed with each other.
classification_rationale: Changelog prose contradicts the code it describes and the commit's own commit message.

trigger: Reading the A5 exceptions ledger row after this diff's edit
summary: The narrowed ledger row read '2026-08-11, narrowed 2026-08-11' - an identical repeated date that reads as a stray duplicate rather than a deliberate same-day narrowing, unlike the file's one other multi-date row which uses two visually distinct dates.
classification_rationale: Clarity nit on an internal compliance ledger; underlying fact was already correct.

trigger: Reading the kOutputSchemaExempt comment block in test_mcp_server.cpp end to end
summary: The comment's first sentence still named DEX+network as part of the 'not yet done' backlog, directly contradicted by a later sentence in the same comment block stating DEX+network is no longer exempt.
classification_rationale: Comment self-contradicts within the same paragraph; the code (the set contents) sides with the later sentence.

trigger: Reading the new structuredContent test's comment against the actual handler code it describes
summary: Comment said get_dex_perf_fleet routes through 'plain tool_result()'; the shared dispatch block actually routes all four of its tools through tool_result_split(), with get_dex_perf_fleet simply passing structured_payload==payload. Behavior described was correct; the named mechanism was not.
classification_rationale: Test comment names the wrong helper function for the code path it documents.

trigger: Comparing get_dex_perf_cohorts' schema (which documents the omitted-when-suppressed nuance via a description field) against the structurally identical get_dex_perf_cohort_diff and get_dex_app_perf/get_dex_group_app_perf schemas (which did not)
summary: 1 of 3 sibling schemas sharing the identical suppression-gated-omission pattern carried the clarifying description; the other two did not. Not a truth defect (nothing in required falsely claims always-present), a documentation-completeness/consistency gap. Found independently by docs-writer and architect.
classification_rationale: Schema remained technically correct either way; the annotation gap is a thoroughness inconsistency across sibling schemas in the same commit.

trigger: A future edit narrowing output_schema_json to nullptr, or misrouting the shared ternary/wrap logic, for list_dex_signals, get_dex_signal_scope, or get_dex_perf_cohort_diff specifically
summary: list_dex_signals/get_dex_signal_scope's existing [pg]-tagged tests and get_dex_perf_cohort_diff's test all used mcp_tool_payload(), which only parses content[0].text and never reads structuredContent - so the new wrap logic for these 3 tools had zero runtime assertion coverage anywhere, even though manual code inspection confirmed all 3 were correct today. Found independently by quality-engineer, security-guardian, and cpp-expert (3 independent reporters). No false-green - the tests just didn't look at the new field.
classification_rationale: Bounded-blast-radius missing coverage per the standing SHOULD rule, not a policy floor; fixed anyway since the fix was small.

trigger: A regression that drops stats from every cohort in structuredContent (not just the suppressed one) - legal because tool_result_split lets content_text and structured_payload diverge
summary: The cohorts leg of the new fleet+cohorts structuredContent test never asserted full content==structuredContent equality, and never positively checked the unsuppressed cohort's stats were present. Fixed: added the equality check and a positive presence check.
classification_rationale: Bounded-blast-radius missing coverage, not a policy floor.

trigger: Two empty arrays trivially satisfy the equality-only check in the new network devices structuredContent test
summary: The new list_network_devices structuredContent test checked equality but never pinned the array size, unlike its DEX-devices sibling test. Fixed: added a size==1 assertion matching the single seeded device.
classification_rationale: Bounded-blast-radius missing coverage, not a policy floor.

waiver_rationale: Negligible cost (small array sizes: DEX signal/scope rollups, not per-device fleet-scale data); restructuring for a double string-copy is not worth the diff churn.
trigger: list_dex_signals/get_dex_signal_scope's wrap call sites each call arr.str() twice (once for content_text, once wrapped for structured_payload)
summary: Each call produces a fresh independent string copy of the same small array buffer; correct, negligible-cost, deliberately not restructured.
classification_rationale: Correct behavior, negligible performance cost on small payloads.

waiver_rationale: Not a defect - a forward-looking design question from batch 1's governance run, explicitly answered here rather than acted on.
summary: Batch 1's governance run asked whether DEX+network's cohort-floor/suppression sibling-flag shapes would need a third structuredContent helper. Revisited: moot for this batch - every sibling-flag (suppressed, found_a/found_b, audit_persisted) is resolved inside the payload-construction JObj/JArr chain before the string reaches tool_result()/tool_result_split(), unlike batch 1's 5 bespoke tools which carry envelope-level siblings alongside content. The third-helper need remains real but stays scoped to batch 1's own tools.
classification_rationale: Answers an open question from the prior governance run; no code change implied.
